summary: Initial integration discovery: Nebula evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key focus on unified SDK compatibility (LangChain / LlamaIndex), gateway vs sidecar proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas per-customer and per-route, and observability hooks (OpenTelemetry + traces). Customer asked about pilot pricing, SOC2/KMS, VPC peering, and canary rollouts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and pilot config; schedule on-prem deep-dive.
topics: Private deployment options: VPC peering, on-prem air-gapped, KMS
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood AE, with Maya our solutions engineer. Quick intro?
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: yeah hi i'm Liam CTO at Nebula, we run platform and infra for our search and summarization product. Priya handles platform and Diego is SRE.
[00:15] Maya Chen: great thanks. today we wanted to understand your integration constraints — are you thinking SDK integration or a gateway/proxy first approach?
[00:28] Priya Rao: primarily we want something that plugs into our existing ingestion pipelines. we use Python microservices, a Node edge proxy, and several LangChain-based orchestration scripts for routing prompts. so SDKs matter to us.
[00:42] Diego Morales: and from ops perspective we need clear rate limiting and quotas per customer org, plus good tracing. we don't want blind spots.
[00:50] Jordan Blake: totally makes sense. quick high-level: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). SDKs (python/node/go) + adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex are first-class — they provide wrapper calls, streaming support, and helper prompts.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: when you say adapter for LangChain, is that a direct connector or an example integration? we've hacked things before and some adapter code falls behind.
[01:20] Maya Chen: good question — it's shipped as an official connector in the SDK and we maintain it; it handles chunking, streaming tokens, and provides retriever plumbing for LlamaIndex. there are examples for both so teams don't reinvent batching and cache patterns.
[01:34] Priya Rao: can the SDK be used behind our own gateway? we want to keep single egress point for auditing.
[01:40] Maya Chen: yes, you can either call Redwood from your services (SDK) or route through a sidecar/gateway. common patterns: 1) SDK in app (simpler), 2) sidecar that handles caching and KV prefix, 3) central gateway/proxy for multi-tenant routing and billing. each has tradeoffs.
[01:56] Diego Morales: how about latency — if we put a sidecar on the same node vs central gateway, what's the latency cost and token efficiency?
[02:06] Maya Chen: sidecar on-node is lowest network latency but you lose pooling across nodes; central gateway enables better batching which reduces per-token cost but can add 20-60ms depending on network and batch windows. for your use-case (real-time chat + async summarization) we typically recommend hybrid: edge-sidecar for low-latency calls and central gateway for bulk/async jobs.
[02:28] Liam O'Connor: curious about quotas — we need per-customer hard quotas and then per-route soft throttles. does Redwood support that out of the box or is it a config we run in our gateway?
[02:40] Jordan Blake: Redwood has per-api-key quota enforcement at the control plane — you can set token/month or request/minute per key and attach metadata tags (customer-id, team). Additionally, if you run a gateway, you can enforce route-specific soft throttles and let Redwood handle failover to lower-cost model variants when quota is hit.
[02:58] Priya Rao: and billing? we need per-tenant cost attribution at token level, ideally exported to our billing system.
[03:06] Maya Chen: yes token-level usage and per-route breakdowns are available via our billing APIs and console CSV export. we also have webhooks for usage events you can ingest.
[03:15] Diego Morales: observability — we use OpenTelemetry and Jaeger. can we get traces with token granularity and link to our spans?
[03:24] Maya Chen: Redwood emits trace contexts and supports OpenTelemetry headers so you can correlate traces. we also surface token counts and model cost in the span attributes. there are a few caveats with streaming where partial responses generate incremental spans — we can show how to stitch them.
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: security — SOC2, KMS, and VPC peering. we have strict data residency and need to use our KMS for key management in private deploys.
[03:50] Jordan Blake: yes, SOC2 and ISO docs are in our security pack. for Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM and we support VPC peering or customer-managed networking for on-prem. air-gapped options require extra setup but are supported.
[04:05] Priya Rao: can the private control plane still push model updates but keep data in our VPC?
[04:11] Maya Chen: yes—control plane can be out-of-band with model artifacts pulled into your environment, or you can run a fully private control plane in your VPC that we install. there are multiple modes depending on compliance.
[04:22] Jordan Blake: maybe to get practical, what's a minimal pilot you'd want?
[04:27] Liam O'Connor: 2-week pilot, run our LangChain workflows against a Dedicated pool to check latency and cost. need 1k-2k requests/day, some streaming chat tests, and a few async batch jobs for reranking.
[04:38] Maya Chen: sounds good. we can provision a small dedicated pool and give you API keys scoped to the pilot with quota and usage export.
[04:46] Diego Morales: one more — fallback behavior. if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can you auto-fail to hosted or a lower-cost quantized model?
[04:54] Jordan Blake: yes, routing policies allow automatic fallback to compatible variants or queued burst capacity. you can set SLOs where critical routes get priority.
[05:03] Priya Rao: what's the connector story for LlamaIndex? we heavily use its retrievers and index store.
[05:09] Maya Chen: our LlamaIndex adapter supports passing retriever objects and will handle batched retrieval + prompt templating. note: sometimes transcription or doc names get mangled — the adapter tolerates missing metadata but we recommend a small eval set to ensure retrieval fidelity.
[05:25] Liam O'Connor: if we route through a central gateway, do you support token-level caching on the gateway or is that Redwood-side?
[05:33] Maya Chen: both — gateway can cache prefixes and responses; Redwood has KV prefix caching to avoid re-computation. best practice is 1) short-term gateway cache for hot prefixes, 2) Redwood-side KV cache for model-stateful caches like KV cache for autoregressive decoders.
[05:50] (crosstalk) Speaker 3: mhm yep
[05:55] Jordan Blake: worth calling out quotas again: you can attach tags so your billing exports produce per-tenant rows; and you can enforce throttles in the gateway to guard spend.
[06:05] Priya Rao: what about SDK credential rotation and SSO? we use SAML and short-lived certs on services.
[06:12] Maya Chen: SDK supports short-lived tokens via our token exchange flow and integrates with SAML/OIDC for enterprise SSO. rotation endpoints and CLI tooling are provided.
[06:22] Diego Morales: for observability — do you have a drop-in middleware or do we need to instrument each service?
[06:28] Maya Chen: we have middleware for common frameworks (express, fastapi) that injects tracing and emits token metrics. for custom runtimes you can call our telemetry APIs directly.
[06:38] Liam O'Connor: latency numbers — can you give an example P95 for a chat convo on Dedicated in us-west?
[06:45] Maya Chen: P95 is typically ~120-180ms for short responses on A10-class Dedicated when using in-region serving and sidecar; central gateway adds 20-60ms depending on batching. for longer generation it's dominated by decoding time.
[06:58] Jordan Blake: ok, let me summarize and capture actions: we'll send SOC2 + security pack, Maya will prepare a Dedicated pilot config and pricing, and Priya will share traffic profile. also schedule a private on-prem deep-dive.
[07:12] Priya Rao: sounds good. also can you share examples of LangChain adapter code? we've seen variants.
[07:18] Maya Chen: yes will share repo links and a short sample notebook.
[07:22] Diego Morales: one oddball question — if we do aggressive quantization to save cost, how do you measure hallucination/regression risk?
[07:29] Maya Chen: we recommend evaluation harnesses—Redwood Optimize runs prompt-level quality checks and regression alerts. for pilots we run side-by-side A/B with golden prompts to track fidelity drop.
[07:41] Liam O'Connor: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:44] Jordan Blake: thanks — we'll follow up via email with the attachments.
[07:49] (meeting ended)
